newsitem.title: GERMANY: Witness in Iran trial in Berlin wants protection.
newsitem.headline: Witness in Iran trial in Berlin wants protection.

text.p: Prosecutors on Monday applied to a Berlin court to bar the public and media when a key witness is heard later this week in the trial of five men suspected of carrying out political assassinations on Iran's orders.

Prosecutor Ronald Georg said the witness, once a top Iranian official, would be in grave danger if identified because he had direct knowledge of the Iranian leadership's alleged involvement in political assassinations and attacks.

The court has spent almost three years hearing evidence in the trial of four Lebanese and an Iranian on suspicion of shooting dead three exiled Iranian Kurdish leaders and their translator in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant in September 1992.

The case prompted the German justice authorities to issue an arrest warrant for Iranian Intelligence Minister Ali Fallahiyan in March and has strained relations between Bonn and Iran, which denies any involvement.
Georg said the defector would take the witness stand only if his identity was protected in a closed-doors session.
The man, who was due to testify on Thursday and Friday, fled Iran after being sentenced to death, the prosecutors' written application said. It did not give further details.
Georg said the man's name had been put forward by Iranian ex-president Abolhassan Banisadr, the prosecution's star witness, who testified in August under heavy security.

Iran was also angered when Banisadr, an enemy of Tehran since fleeing in 1981, said religious leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei ordered the killings and President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani signed the order.
